title: The abelianity conjecture for special compact Kähler manifolds
main_claim: Every special connected compact Kähler manifold has a virtually abelian fundamental group, which resolves Campana's abelianity conjecture in all dimensions. As corollaries, π1 is virtually abelian when κ=0, Conjecture S / bimeromorphic Iitaka uniformization hold, and the universal cover of a special manifold is holomorphically convex.

issues.description: This is the analytic engine of the nonamenable branch, and it is a new and strong result: zero lies in the Dolbeault (p,0) spectrum of every infinite normal cover of a compact Kähler orbifold. I checked these steps and found them consistent: the Poincaré-to-L^2 mass bound ||u_N||≤CN^n; the depth argument; the cell count C N^{2n}; the Bochner-Kodaira weighted inverse bound C(e^{b/4}+√t e^{b/2}) and the quadratic μ(μ+Ct)≥δ²e^{-b}; the weight curvature bound and the deep-region value h=N; the S-scaling of the smoothing estimate; and the final decay N^{2n-r/6}. I did not fully re-derive the global Monge-Ampère continuity on the complete cover, or the uniform Demailly-Kollár exponent over the normalized family. Nothing failed, but the whole theorem rests on this unrefereed analytic argument.
issues.evidence: Theorem: '...For some p in {0,...,n}, zero belongs to the spectrum of the L^2 Dolbeault Laplacian on scalar (p,0)-forms on U'

issues.description: Both branches finish with cited external theorems that I did not check against the sources: Campana-Păun Thm 7.11 used without any pseudoeffectivity hypothesis; Boucksom's volume criterion, where a positive current whose absolutely continuous part is strictly positive on an open set is taken to give bigness; and CCE Thms 1/6.3 (torsion-free, Zariski-dense image into a simple group giving a Shafarevich base of general type). If any citation needs extra hypotheses, the corresponding branch needs repair. The paper's paraphrases match the standard forms of these results as I know them.
issues.evidence: 'The big-line criterion for orbifold cotangent tensors [CampanaPaun2019, Theorem 7.11] now implies that K_Y+Δ is big... No pseudoeffectivity assumption is needed in that criterion.'

coverage:
I read all of introduction, preliminaries, spectral, hilbert, descent and completion in build/sections, and checked the logic step by step:
- Lemma torus-divisor; finite-by-abelian and realize-finite-index lemmas.
- Albanese exactness, including the inertia-divisibility and small-ample-boundary Bogomolov-sheaf argument.
- FAb of N: the inflation-restriction, B. Wang isolated-torsion, isogeny-relabel and transgression-injectivity steps.
- Proposition minimal-base: the dimension squeeze and the derivation of (M).
- Torus descent: the Iitaka fibre, Albanese-exceptional boundary, torus-bundle model, equivariant comparison, birational pushdown and neat pullback.
- Hilbert section: the ultrapower and Shalom constructions, Plücker line tensor, the minimal-rank argument with the finite-Ad trick making J° abelian, the spectral-fibre rank drop, discreteness, and the compact-fibre Γ-dimension bound.
- Spectral section: estimates and exponents checked by hand.
- The linear branch: Selberg and generic largeness via minimality.
- Corollaries 1.2-1.5 checked briefly.
I did not consult the cited external sources, and did not fully redo the Monge-Ampère a priori estimates.
